problem_text:
A logistics firm must coordinate inspection visits to nine distinct regional facilities, whose geographical positions are provided as planar coordinates:
Facility Alpha: (77,197)
Facility Beta: (104,98)
Facility Gamma: (98,15)
Facility Delta: (41,164)
Facility Epsilon: (32,61)
Facility Zeta: (73,186)
Facility Theta: (85,14)
Facility Eta: (9,123)
Facility Iota: (106,36)

The travel distances between facilities, measured in kilometers, are precomputed as follows:
Alpha to Gamma: 183.2 km
Alpha to Delta: 48.8 km
Alpha to Epsilon: 143.3 km
Alpha to Zeta: 11.7 km
Alpha to Theta: 183.2 km
Alpha to Eta: 100.5 km
Alpha to Iota: 163.6 km
Beta to Gamma: 83.2 km
Beta to Delta: 91.2 km
Beta to Epsilon: 81.0 km
Beta to Zeta: 93.3 km
Beta to Theta: 86.1 km
Beta to Eta: 98.2 km
Beta to Iota: 62.0 km
Gamma to Delta: 159.5 km
Gamma to Epsilon: 80.4 km
Gamma to Zeta: 172.8 km
Gamma to Theta: 13.0 km
Gamma to Eta: 139.9 km
Gamma to Iota: 22.5 km
Delta to Epsilon: 103.4 km
Delta to Zeta: 38.8 km
Delta to Theta: 156.3 km
Delta to Eta: 52.0 km
Delta to Iota: 143.6 km
Epsilon to Zeta: 131.6 km
Epsilon to Theta: 70.8 km
Epsilon to Eta: 66.1 km
Epsilon to Iota: 78.1 km
Zeta to Theta: 172.4 km
Zeta to Eta: 89.8 km
Zeta to Iota: 153.6 km
Theta to Eta: 132.9 km
Theta to Iota: 30.4 km
Eta to Iota: 130.3 km

Direct travel between Facility Alpha and Facility Beta is not permitted due to a permanent route obstruction. Furthermore, the inspection circuit must incorporate exactly one of two critical connector routes: either the link between Beta and Gamma, or the link between Gamma and Delta.

The objective is to determine the minimal total travel distance for a closed inspection tour that visits every facility precisely once before returning to the point of origin.
